items.title: Porter's framework asks about industry structure, not firms
items.claim: Michael Porter's 1979 HBR article introduced the five forces framework. What does it analyse?

options.text: The structural attractiveness of an industry: rivalry, bargaining power of buyers, bargaining power of suppliers, threat of new entrants, threat of substitutes

items.reveal:
Porter's 'How Competitive Forces Shape Strategy' (HBR, March 1979) made a structural argument: average industry profitability is set by the strength of the five forces. Some industries (pharma, software platforms) are persistently profitable; others (airlines, supermarkets) persistently low-margin.

McGahan and Porter (1997) found industry effects explained 19% of business unit profitability variance — less than firm effects (32%) but real. Critics (including Henry Mintzberg) argue the framework underweights innovation, complementors and network effects, which 1979 industry economics didn't see clearly.
items.why: Strategy starts with which industry you're competing in, not how cleverly you compete. Some industries make it nearly impossible to earn supernormal returns.

items.title: Blockbuster could have bought Netflix for $50 million in 2000
items.claim: In 2000, Netflix was a struggling DVD-by-mail service. What did Blockbuster's CEO John Antioco do when Reed Hastings flew to Dallas to propose a sale?

options.text: Agreed in principle but the deal collapsed over terms
Laughed Hastings out of the room
Counter-offered to buy Netflix for $200 million
Bought a minority stake to monitor the technology

items.reveal_title: The room where it didn't happen
items.reveal:
Reed Hastings and Marc Randolph have both told the story (Randolph's book 'That Will Never Work' has the most colour). They proposed Blockbuster acquire Netflix for $50 million and run blockbuster.com as the online arm. Antioco — facing a profitable late-fee business model — declined.

Blockbuster did later launch an online service (Blockbuster Online) and was on a recovery path under Antioco, but a 2005 boardroom fight with activist investor Carl Icahn led to Antioco's departure and the strategy's reversal. Blockbuster filed for bankruptcy in 2010.

Netflix's market cap is now over $300 billion.
items.why: Disruption isn't usually about technology incumbents can't access; it's about business models they can't bring themselves to attack. Late fees were too profitable to risk.

items.title: Decline is not the end — vinyl records came back
items.claim: Vinyl record sales collapsed from the mid-1980s as CDs took over. What has happened since the late 2000s?

options.text: Vinyl sales have risen every year from 2007 to 2023, overtaking CDs in US revenue terms in 2022 for the first time since 1987 (RIAA data)

items.reveal:
RIAA US data: vinyl revenue fell to under $20m by 2006. By 2022, vinyl revenue was $1.2bn — overtaking CDs ($483m) for the first time in 35 years. UK Official Charts data shows similar pattern from 2008 onwards.

The textbook PLC implies decline is terminal. Brand repositioning, nostalgia and physical-product premiums in a streaming world reversed that trajectory. Other examples: Polaroid film, Kodak Super 8, mechanical watches.
items.why: The four-stage product life cycle is a framework, not a law of nature. Decline can be reversed by changing what the product means to customers.
